IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON KNOWLEDGE AND DATA ENGINEERING, VOL. XX, NO. XX, OCTOBER 2026

DocuTrust: Multi-Agent Evidence Governance, Policy Version Precedence, and Calibrated Abstention for Compliance Question Answering

DocuTrust Research Consortium
Correspondence: docutrust-research@example.org • Open-source reproducibility repository: https://github.com/docutrust/research

Abstract—Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems deployed in enterprise regulatory, legal, and operational compliance environments face strict trustworthiness criteria that standard semantic search cannot satisfy: responses must strictly adhere to currently active policy versions, resolve contradictory rules across heterogeneous manuals, verify that every generated assertion is entailed by cited evidence, and safely abstain when documentation is absent. In this work, we conduct an extensive systematic literature review (66 screened records, 56 included primary studies, and 27 deeply synthesized evidence matrix entries) and present DocuTrust, an evidence-governed multi-agent architecture designed specifically for compliance question answering. DocuTrust integrates: (1) calibrated hybrid retrieval combining lexical BM25 and dense FAISS embeddings with cross-encoder neural reranking, (2) dynamic policy version supersession resolution preventing outdated clause contamination, (3) typed clause-level cross-document contradiction detection with authority hierarchy arbitration, (4) sentence-level claim verification via natural language inference, (5) calibrated multi-factor evidence confidence routing with human-review escalation, and (6) SHA-256 cryptographic provenance receipts. We evaluate DocuTrust against five baseline paradigms and five systematic ablations across 408 executed inference runs on DocuTrust-Bench, an independently audited multi-domain test collection spanning Information Security, Data Privacy, Corporate Finance, and Remote Work policies (50 annotated queries with zero-leakage splits). On the frozen test set (N=34), DocuTrust achieves an MRR of 0.878 (nDCG@8 = 0.910), a Claim Support Rate of 91.7%, and a Cross-Document Conflict F1 of 85.7% (compared to 0.0% for all standard RAG baselines). On unanswerable compliance inquiries (N=8), DocuTrust achieves a 100.0% Safe Non-Answer Rate (8/8 queries safely routed to abstention or human escalation, preventing ungrounded hallucination), while maintaining an exact 3-way decision concordance of 44.1% with a 53.8% False Abstention Rate reflecting enterprise compliance-first conservatism. An independent scientific audit confirmed zero test-set data leakage, resolved experimental timing anomalies, and verified full result reproducibility.

Index Terms—Retrieval-augmented generation, compliance question answering, evidence governance, claim verification, policy version precedence, calibrated abstention, systematic literature review, cryptographic provenance, multi-agent architectures.

I. Introduction

Enterprise and government institutions operate within complex, evolving regulatory environments, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) [26], NIST SP 800-53 [27], ISO 27001 [28], and internal administrative codes. In compliance question answering (Compliance-QA), automated responses directly guide employee authorizations, cryptographic controls, breach disclosures, and expense claims. Consequently, an inaccurate, outdated, or hallucinated answer carries severe liabilities: regulatory enforcement fines, data leaks, corporate fraud, and audit failures.

While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [1] has become the standard paradigm for grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) on private corpora, standard RAG architectures exhibit four fundamental failure modes in compliance settings:

  1. Temporal & Policy Supersession Failures: Corporate manuals undergo continuous versioning (e.g., v1.0 → v2.0). Semantic vector search regularly retrieves superseded clauses because obsolete text shares high embedding similarity with active rules, leading models to quote revoked allowances.
  2. Authority Hierarchy Blindness: Compliance rules follow rigid authority tiers (statute > corporate code > departmental guideline > manager discretion). Conventional RAG treats retrieved passages as flat text, failing to detect when an employee's informal email approval violates an overarching corporate policy mandate.
  3. Hallucination on Absent Rules: When inquiries address unestablished topics (e.g., unauthorized reimbursement categories or unsupported international jurisdictions), standard LLMs fabricate plausible rules rather than refusing to answer (0.0% appropriate abstention in naive RAG).
  4. Absence of Immutable Audit Provenance: Formal compliance requires verifiable, tamper-evident audit receipts linking answers to specific cryptographic chunk hashes and active policy versions.

To overcome these limitations, we present DocuTrust, an evidence-governed multi-agent compliance intelligence architecture. Unlike single-pass retrieve-and-generate pipelines, DocuTrust decomposes compliance question answering into specialized verification stages: dual-index hybrid retrieval, dynamic version intelligence, typed cross-document conflict analysis, sentence-level NLI claim verification, calibrated confidence routing, and cryptographic SHA-256 provenance signing.

Fig. 1. DocuTrust end-to-end multi-agent evidence governance architecture. Solid borders denote verified implemented modules in the operational repository; dashed borders denote proposed/extended pipeline interfaces. The system coordinates document chunking, hybrid retrieval, neural reranking, active-version filtering, evidence sufficiency checking, cross-document conflict analysis, sentence-level NLI verification, calibrated confidence routing, and SHA-256 provenance receipt signing.

II. Systematic Literature Review

We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review [29] investigating evidence retrieval, claim-level attribution, and safe abstention. Across five databases (ACL Anthology, arXiv.org, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus), exactly 66 candidate records were screened (Fig. 2). During full-text evaluation, 10 records were excluded under transparent criteria: lacks citation/attribution evaluation (E1, n=2), theoretical without retrieval evaluation (E2, n=2), extended abstracts (E3, n=2), superseded preprints (E4, n=2), and inaccessible full text (E5, n=2). Exactly 56 primary studies met all inclusion criteria, with 27 synthesized into our deep evidence matrix.

Fig. 2. PRISMA 2020 flow diagram illustrating the systematic literature screening process, reconciled against the verified screening repository (LITERATURE_SCREENING.csv). Exactly 56 studies met all inclusion criteria, with 27 analyzed in the evidence matrix.
Fig. 3. Taxonomy of trustworthy compliance question answering derived from the systematic synthesis of 56 included studies across five core pillars: Evidence Retrieval & Hybrid Fusion, Temporal Governance & Precedence, Sentence-Level Claim Verification, Calibrated Abstention & Fallback, and Cryptographic Audit Provenance.

Our systematic synthesis structured the literature into five core pillars (Fig. 3): (1) Evidence Retrieval & Hybrid Fusion: While dense retrievers (DPR [2], REALM [3], RETRO [4]) excel in general QA, compliance corpora require combining BM25 [5] and dense vectors via RRF [6] with neural reranking [7]. (2) Temporal Governance: Explicit version constraints are essential to resolve policy supersession [21]. (3) Sentence-Level Verification: Decomposing answers into atomic propositions for NLI entailment checking (FActScore [13], TRUE [14], AIS [10], RARR [12]). (4) Calibrated Abstention: Selective classification [17] and semantic entropy [16] provide risk-coverage guarantees against hallucination [18, 19]. (5) Cryptographic Provenance: Generating tamper-evident receipts to protect against prompt injection [25] and guarantee audit verifiability [24]. Table I provides a detailed capability comparison.

III. The DocuTrust Architecture

DocuTrust operates as a multi-stage deterministic pipeline:

A. Calibrated Hybrid Retrieval & Neural Reranking

Candidate chunks are retrieved from BM25 lexical search (sBM25) and dense FAISS vectors (sdense, all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and fused using Reciprocal Rank Fusion:

RRF(d) = ∑m [60 + rankm(d)]−1 (1)

The top candidates (K=8) are reranked by a neural cross-encoder (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2). Cross-encoder logits are normalized via sigmoid scaling: Scal = σ(logit). When the cross-encoder is ablated, pooled RRF scores are dynamically calibrated to prevent score compression:

ScalRRF = min(1.0, max(0.1, 0.95 · [sraw / max(spool, 2/61)] · [1 + 0.08(r − 1)]−1)) (2)

B. Dynamic Policy Version Precedence

Retrieved chunks are filtered via get_active_version() to eliminate superseded policy versions prior to evidence generation. Chunks follow strict IDs: ⟨doc_id⟩_p⟨page⟩_c⟨idx⟩, preventing version collision.

C. Cross-Document Policy Conflict Analysis

Passages are parsed into typed PolicyClause tuples: ⟨doc_id, ver, section, scope, modality, value⟩, where modality ∈ {MANDATORY, PROHIBITED, PERMITTED, EXCEPTION}. Normative conflicts are detected whenever informal discretion or outdated clauses contradict formal governing ceilings.

D. Sentence-Level Claim Verification

Candidate answers are partitioned into claims {c1, ..., cm}. Each claim is checked for NLI entailment against evidence:

supported(ci) = ∃ e ∈ ℰ : PNLI(Entailment | e, ci) ≥ 0.85 (3)

Claim Support Rate (CSR) is computed as ∑ supported(ci) / m. If m=0, CSR is reported as N/A.

E. Calibrated Confidence Routing & Audit Receipts

Routing decisions ŷ ∈ {ANSWER, ESCALATE_REVIEW, ABSTAIN} are governed by:

Ω = 0.25 R + 0.25 C + 0.20 A + 0.30 V − 0.35 Iconflict (4)

If Ω ≥ 0.70 → ANSWER; if 0.40 ≤ Ω < 0.70 → ESCALATE_REVIEW; if Ω < 0.40 → ABSTAIN. Every completed interaction generates an immutable SHA-256 provenance receipt (Fig. 4).

Fig. 4. Conceptual evidence-provenance chain linking source policy chunks, generated claims, NLI entailment scores, and cryptographic SHA-256 receipts.

IV. The DocuTrust-Bench Benchmark

To evaluate compliance QA under realistic enterprise conditions, we created DocuTrust-Bench (Fig. 5), comprising four document families (Security, Privacy, Remote Work, and Finance) and 50 annotated queries. The dataset enforces strict zero-leakage domain isolation:

  • Development Set (N=16): Mapped strictly to the Civilian Work-From-Home policy. Used solely for parameter tuning.
  • Frozen Test Set (N=34): Mapped across Security (n=12), Privacy (n=11), and Finance (n=11) policies.
  • Zero Overlap: Corpus(Dev) ∩ Corpus(Test) = ∅.

The test split contains 26 answerable queries and 8 unanswerable out-of-scope queries.

Fig. 5. DocuTrust-Bench evaluation protocol and split architecture. The development set (N=16) is completely disjoint from the frozen test set (N=34), ensuring zero document data leakage.

A. Retrieval Efficacy

Dense-only retrieval (BASE-B) performs poorly on regulatory text, achieving an MRR of 0.779 and Hit@1 of 61.5% due to exact alphanumeric code mismatches. BM25 achieves an MRR of 0.865. Hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder reranking (BASE-D and SYS-FULL) achieves the highest retrieval performance: MRR = 0.878 and nDCG@8 = 0.910 (Fig. 6).

B. Safe Abstention vs. Hallucination

On unanswerable queries (N=8), unverified baselines (BASE-A..D) hallucinated fabricated answers on every instance (0.0% Safe Non-Answer Rate). In contrast, DocuTrust achieved a 100.0% Safe Non-Answer Rate (8/8 queries safely routed to ABSTAIN or ESCALATE_REVIEW). Under exact 3-way decision matching (Fig. 7), DocuTrust achieves a 44.1% accuracy with a 53.8% False Abstention Rate on answerable queries, reflecting an enterprise-first posture where human escalation is favored over hallucination.

Fig. 7. Left: 3-way confusion matrix for SYS-FULL (exact concordance = 15/34 = 44.1%). Right: Compliance safety tradeoff: achieving 100% safe non-answering on unanswerable inputs with 53.8% false abstention on borderline inputs.

C. Conflict Detection

Standard prompt baselines achieved 0.0% Conflict F1, missing all three test conflicts. DocuTrust achieved an 85.7% Conflict F1 (Precision = 75.0%, Recall = 100.0%).

D. Component Ablation Analysis

Table III and Fig. 8 present the ablation results. Removing claim verification (ABL-1) degrades 3-way decision accuracy to 32.4% and spikes false abstentions to 69.2%. Removing conflict analysis (ABL-3) collapses Conflict F1 from 85.7% to 0.0%. Removing neural reranking (ABL-5) drops MRR from 0.878 to 0.860.

E. Latency Analysis: Unmasking the BM25 Cold Start

Initial benchmarks reported an anomalous BM25 mean latency of 1,847.4 ms. Our audit revealed this was an experimental cold-start artifact (Fig. 9, left): Query #1 incurred a one-time index loading penalty of 40,223.6 ms (40.2 s). For Queries 2--34, BM25 exhibited a steady-state median latency of 0.5 ms. DocuTrust (SYS-FULL) exhibits a steady-state median latency of 236.0 ms (mean = 237.8 ms). Neural cross-encoder reranking accounts for 221.0 ms (93.6%), hybrid retrieval takes 14.0 ms (5.9%), and governance verification executes in 1.0 ms (0.5%) (Fig. 9, right).

Fig. 9. Latency analysis. Left: Comparison of mean vs. steady-state median latency unmasking BM25's 40.2s cold start. Right: Median latency decomposition for SYS-FULL (236.0 ms total).

F. Statistical Significance

Paired Student's t-tests on MRR (t(25)=1.383, p=0.1787) and nDCG@8 (t(25)=1.377, p=0.1807), as well as McNemar's test on decision accuracy (p=0.3593), confirm directional improvements that do not reach significance at α=0.05 due to benchmark sample size (N=34). The 95% bootstrap CI for SYS-FULL MRR is [0.782, 0.962]; for nDCG@8 it is [0.839, 0.972].

VI. Independent Scientific Audit

An independent audit reviewed all raw execution records (408 trials) and remediated seven findings: (1) eliminated ground-truth oracle active_version leakage; (2) isolated generation caches per configuration; (3) resolved CSR division-by-zero errors; (4) calibrated raw RRF scores; (5) replaced domain-overfitted WFH heuristics with typed PolicyClause rules; (6) implemented exact Student's t and binomial McNemar tests; (7) logged complete cryptographic provenance manifests.

VII. Limitations & Future Work

While achieving 100% safe non-answering on unanswerable inputs, the 53.8% False Abstention Rate reflects an ultra-conservative posture. Future work will explore Bayesian threshold calibration to recover automated coverage without increasing hallucination risk. We are also expanding DocuTrust-Bench from 50 to 400 queries across ten enterprise compliance verticals.

VIII. Conclusion

We presented DocuTrust, an evidence-governed multi-agent compliance intelligence architecture. Supported by an extensive PRISMA systematic review, DocuTrust achieves 100.0% safe non-answering on unanswerable inputs, 85.7% conflict F1, 91.7% claim support, and a steady-state median latency of 236.0 ms, backed by an independent audit and cryptographic SHA-256 provenance receipts.

Reproducibility Statement

All code, datasets, evaluation scripts, raw inference logs (408 records), and independent audit files are available at: https://github.com/docutrust/research.
